title: Contextual Tracing Enrichment and Burn‑Rate Playbooks for Anomaly-driven Paging
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement contextual trace enrichment in our tracing hooks + extend metrics/log pipelines to feed an anomaly detector, and author automated burn-rate playbooks that tie into paging policies. The goal is to reduce noisy pages, speed mean time to context (MTTC), and improve SLO signal fidelity for latency and error budgets.

Background: We currently have tracing hooks wired into request paths and a set of SLO burn-rate alerts. Recent incidents showed (1) high burn-rate pages with insufficient context; (2) noisy pages because threshold rules don't account for correlated downstream errors; and (3) metric/log pipelines that lack normalized fields needed by anomaly models. This ticket builds bridging infra and operational playbooks so oncall receives prioritized, contextual pages backed by automated enrichment.

Success criteria (objective):
- 40% reduction in low-action pages triggered by transient noise (measured month-over-month).
- Median MTTC for pages reduced from ~7min to <=3min in pilot services.
- Burn-rate alerts automatically attach the top 3 correlated traces and a normalized error histogram in the initial page payload.
- Anomaly detector consumes normalized metrics/logs with <30s ingestion lag for critical services.

Workstreams and implementation plan:
1) Tracing hook enrichment (owner: Marco)
   - Extend trace sampler to add derived attributes: service_topology, request_semantic_tag (e.g. api.batch, api.sync), and upstream_error_signature.
   - Add lightweight trace snippet attachment API so alerting can embed 3-span summaries.
   - Backwards-compat: if enrichment fails, fall back to current trace ids (no page failure).

2) Metrics/log pipeline changes (owner: Leah Chen)
   - Normalize error codes, latency buckets, and route tags at the collector stage (Fluent Bit wrapper).
   - Emit a canonical metrics set to observability ingestion topic with consistent naming for anomaly models.
   - Add schema versioning and transformation tests.

3) Anomaly detector integration (owner: Data Infra)
   - Wire the normalized stream to the anomaly service and create a per-service baseline model.
   - Expose a confidence score and top-k contributing features to the alerting subsystem.

4) Burn-rate playbooks and paging automation (owner: Oncall Ops)
   - Define playbooks that map burn-rate severity + anomaly confidence -> paging policy (no page, async slack, or page SRE).
   - Attach automated context (top traces, error histograms, recent deploy metadata) to page payloads.
   - Implement quiet windows and smart de-duplication to avoid alert storms.

5) Dashboards and validation
   - Create a latency/error dashboard that surfaces burn-rate, anomaly conf, and paging outcomes.
   - Run a two-week dark launch on non-customer-critical services, measure signal/noise and MTTC.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Adding enrichment increases collector CPU and storage for short-lived attachments; we limit attachments to 3 spans and TTL them after 24h.
- Anomaly models introduce a degree of false positives early; playbooks initially bias toward non-paging notifications at low confidence.
- Schema changes to pipelines require coordinated rollout with partners; we will version transforms and support v1/v2 ingestion in parallel for 6 weeks.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit + integration tests for sampler enrichment and attachment API.
- End-to-end harness that simulates correlated downstream failures to validate burn-rate + anomaly decisions.
- Dark launch for two weeks on staging -> pilot services -> gradual ramp.

Observability and metrics to monitor post-launch:
- Pages per 1000 burn-rate events (goal: -40% noise).
- Median MTTC and MTTR.
- Attachment delivery success rate (>99%).
- Anomaly ingestion lag and model confidence calibration.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Enrichment may leak sensitive fields. Mitigation: Strict allowlist of trace attributes and PII scrubbers; security review required for any new attribute.
- Risk: Increased alert complexity confuses paging. Mitigation: Clear playbooks and training session with oncall crew before ramp.
